subject: Post-demo: Model fit & quantization tradeoffs (FinWave) - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-demo: Model fit & quantization tradeoffs (FinWave) - next steps

Hi Alice / Bob 

Thanks again for the call today  really helpful to see the FinWave ingest and retrieval flow. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of needs (from discovery):
- Primary goal: generation & extraction over financial filings + analyst notes (high precision for numeric extraction, conservative hallucination profile).
- Throughput: bursts up to ~350 requests/min, steady-state ~80 req/min. Typical prompt + context ~1.5k tokens, expected response ~300 tokens.
- Latency target: p90 < 450 ms for interactive workflows; background batch jobs can be higher.
- Security: data residency in US, KMS-managed keys, SOC2 evidence required.

Suggested model candidates to evaluate:
1) Llama-3 13B (fp16 baseline)  good balance of cost/latency for extraction-heavy tasks.
2) Llama-3 70B (quantized AWQ 4-bit)  target for higher-quality generation while improving throughput.
3) Llama-family with GPTQ 4-bit  better accuracy retention vs some AWQ roots but potentially slower.
4) FP8 exploration on H100 for peak throughput/CUDA-accelerated inference (hardware dependent).

What we'll run for the next evaluation:
- Redwood to run two parallel eval tracks on your prompt set: AWQ 4-bit, GPTQ 4-bit and fp16 baseline. We'll include an FP8 run if you can allow H100-backed nodes.
- Metrics: semantic similarity (embedding cosine), token-level extraction precision/recall, hallucination checks against ground truth, and latency/cost-per-token.
- Deliverables: sample outputs (5-10 representative prompts), benchmark PDF, and a short M.A.P. (mutual action plan) with timelines.

Attachments: I attached the prompt set you shared (finwave_prompt_set_v1.json) and our initial benchmark template (redwood_quant_benchmarks_awq_gptq_fp8.pdf).

Next steps / asks from FinWave:
- Confirm approval to run evals on your production-like data (we will use sandboxed, ephemeral instances; everything stays in your US region).
- Share any minimum quality thresholds (e.g., extraction precision >= 95%) or examples where hits/misses are most costly.
- Availability for a technical deep dive the week of Mar 2  proposed slots Tue/Wed mornings PT. Dev and Marcus will lead.

I'll loop back with a proposed M.A.P. and meeting invite once I hear your availability.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Subject: RE: Post-demo: Model fit & quantization tradeoffs (FinWave) - next steps

Hi team 

Following up with the technical evaluation plan and a few clarifications on quantization tradeoffs (high-level):

Eval config (what we'll run):
- Datasets: finwave_prompt_set_v1.json (you provided) + 200 annotated extraction examples you flagged as high-risk.
- Runs: fp16 baseline (Llama-3 13B), AWQ 4-bit (Llama-3 70B), GPTQ 4-bit (Llama-3 70B). Optional FP8 run on H100 if FinWave approves H100-backed sandbox.
- Metrics:
  * Extraction precision / recall (tight numeric matching),
  * Semantic similarity (embedding cosine, averaged),
  * Hallucination rate (false facts per 1k tokens),
  * Latency (p50/p90) and cost/token (USD).

Quantization notes:
- AWQ (4-bit): typically gives best throughput improvements and lower memory footprint on many open weights; some micro-architectural differences can introduce token-level regressions in edge cases (numerical extraction can be sensitive). We should run focused extraction tests.
- GPTQ (4-bit): often preserves fp16 accuracy more consistently for generation tasks compared to some AWQ variants, but encoding/decoding kernels can be slightly slower  expect ~10-25% lower throughput vs AWQ at same quant width.
- FP8: very promising on H100 with TensorFloat/AMP optimizations  can give both speed and quality benefits but requires matching runtime and is more sensitive to kernel maturity. We'll flag FP8 as exploratory.

Infrastructure & perf expectations:
- For your throughput (bursts ~350 req/min), target pool: 2 x H100-similar instances (or 4 x A100 depending on final model/quant profile) with autoscale for bursts.
- Batching: adaptive batching with a 15-30 ms tail latency cap; we'll tune batch windows per route.

Risk mitigation & eval criteria:
- We'll include a small subset of your critical extraction prompts (10-20) where any regression is considered a blocker.
- If AWQ shows extraction degradation > 2-3% absolute vs fp16 baseline on those critical prompts, we recommend staying on GPTQ or fp16 for that route, or applying post-processing extraction heuristics.

Deliverables:
- Benchmark PDF (attached) with run configs and raw outputs.
- Per-prompt diff view (sample outputs).
- Recommendation: quant profile per route (e.g., generation-heavy routes = AWQ, extraction-heavy routes = GPTQ/fp16 fallback).

I attached the initial benchmark export  will run the full sweep once we get your sign-off to use the supplied data in the sandbox.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com

Thanks Marissa / Dev  good summary. A few clarifying Qs before we sign off on the evals: 

1) Quality thresholds: for numeric extraction we need precision >= 95% and recall >= 92% on the high-risk set  anything below that will create rework for downstream teams. Are those thresholds realistic for AWQ?
2) Examples: Can you include 8-10 side-by-side samples showing fp16 vs AWQ vs GPTQ outputs for both extraction and free-form generation? I want to see where hallucinations show up.
3) Data residency + KMS: Confirm all sandbox runs use US region and our KMS keys (we can provide an account-level key and a test envelope). Also need SOC2 checklist pieces before we share the 200 annotated examples.
4) Cost: ballpark monthly run estimate for the three eval tracks and an estimate for production using AWQ vs GPTQ (assuming 80 req/min steady).

If you can provide the sample outputs and a draft mutual action plan (MAP) we can review this week. We're tentatively available Wed Mar 4 10am PT or Thu Mar 5 11am PT for a follow-up demo.

On the risk point Dev flagged  quoting: 
> If AWQ shows extraction degradation > 2-3% absolute vs fp16 baseline on those critical prompts, we recommend staying on GPTQ or fp16 for that route

That sounds reasonable; we'll want the MAP to include an automatic fallback to a higher-fidelity variant if a production regression is detected.

Thanks,
Alice Smith
Head of ML Platforms | FinWave
alice@finwave.com
